brief.md:
# Next Role - brief for Claude

Read this before changing anything on this board, in any chat or scheduled run.

- **This board is the source of truth** for roles, companies, sectors, people, channels, preferences (`profile/prefs`), profile (`profile/me`), their base CV and letter (`templates/cv`, `templates/letter`; shown as About me › My CV & letter; each has a `text` field with the document as Markdown — the CV text is evidence of their experience: check `profile/skills`, then the CV text, then `profile/me` before calling anything a gap; `profile/me` holds the facts the board uses as settings plus what the CV doesn't say), packs (`packs/<roleId>`) and the versions the user sent (`finals/<roleId>`). Never mirror any of it into another tool.
- **Roles have a number** (`ref`), shown as #N. When the user says "#74", find the role with `ref == 74`. Never write or change `ref`.
- **Every destructive action on the board gets a confirm pop-up.** Rejects need a reason.
- **Cite a rule with its meaning**: its id and name together, "<id> (<name>)", never a bare id.
- **Which board:** work on the board the scheduled task or the request names; otherwise the one in the project instructions. A request about another board (a test board) uses that board for everything in it.
- **Every date field is `YYYY-MM-DD`.** Never text, a placeholder or a guess: leave it empty if unknown. A malformed date breaks parts of the board.
- **`url` is a web address** starting `http://` or `https://`, or empty.
- **Board code:** the runtime's `db` namespace is frozen - never mutate it, wrap it. Test page changes before publishing.
- **Packs are Word files stored as base64** in `packs/<roleId>` ({cv, letter} each {name, size, sha256, b64}). The role keeps `pack` with `stored: "board"`. The pack is a starting draft: the user finishes it in Word or a Claude chat, and asks for a revision in chat ("revise the pack for #N: …"). The versions the user sent are in `finals/<roleId>` ({cv, letter}, same shape, Word or PDF), with a small `final` summary on the role ({cv, letter} each {name, size, at}); they are their uploads, read-only to every skill, and interview prep works from them. `packNotes` is retired.

## Words on the board

Use these names when talking to the user and in every report. The stored field names don't change. **Never say Gate 1 or Gate 2**: it is the longlist and the shortlist.

| Say | Stored as | Means |
|---|---|---|
| **Deal-breakers** | `prefs.hardRules`, `enrich.gate2Rules` (G codes) | Fail one and it's a no |
| **Preferences** | `prefs.scored`, `highlights`, `enrich.expensive` (S codes) | Rated Strong / Middle / Weak, never added up |
| **Concerns** | `red` | Worth knowing, not a no. About what the user wants from the role — never a requirement of theirs the user doesn't meet: that is a Role Fit gap or partial in `fit.reqs` |
| **Pluses** | `green`, `prefs.upside` | Bonus points. About what the user wants — never a requirement the user meets: that is Role Fit evidence in `fit.reqs` |
| **My criteria** ("Me") | the four above | How the role fits what the user wants: Strong, Mixed (a weak preference) or Fails (a deal-breaker failed) |
| **Their criteria** ("Them") | `fit` | How the user fits what they want: Role Fit, a % and band |
| **Research log** | `g2Note` | How the shortlist run gathered its research; not a decision |
| **Longlist** (was Gate 1) | `stage: "proposed"`; dropped = `g1_rejected`; `g1At`, `g1Reason`, `g1Note` | New roles from the sweep — the gut check |
| **Shortlist** (was Gate 2) | `stage: "consideration"` (or `parked`); dropped = `g2_rejected`; `g2At`, `g2Note`, `enrich.gate2Rules` | Researched roles to decide on |
| **Dropped from longlist / shortlist** | `g1_rejected` / `g2_rejected`; `endStage` stays "Gate 1" / "Gate 2" | The board shows the new words |
| **CV** (was Pack, and Sent once applied) | `packs/<roleId>`, the role's `pack`; what was sent = `finals/<roleId>`, the role's `final`; task kind `pack` | The tailored CV and cover letter for a role. Say "the CV" or "CV and cover letter", never "pack" |
| **Ruled out** (was Off the list) | company `listing`: `rejected` (not for you), `excluded` (fails a deal-breaker) or `defunct` (employer may be gone); `offNote`, `offAt` | A company whose roles are screened out from every source and whose board is never fetched. Set from its rating or when rejecting a role there; a company with no card gets a bare one (`createdVia: "rejection"`). Never say "off the list" |

Role card tabs keep one order at every stage: Overview · Fit · CV · Interviews · Questions · Company · Notes. A tab appears only when it applies (CV from To apply on; Interviews from the shortlist on).

About me › My criteria is where the user edits their deal-breakers, preferences, concerns, pluses and search terms (`profile/prefs`).

**Deal-breaker types.** Every deal-breaker (`hardRules`) carries a `type` saying what it is about: `pay`, `office`, `location`, `rtw` (right to work), `contract` (permanent, fixed-term, temporary, contractor or freelance, fractional, part-time), `hours` (working window, on-call, shifts), `level`, `roletype` (title and function), `sector` (sector and domain, ethics included), `company` (size or stage), `employer` (named companies) or `other`. Preferences (`scored`) may carry one too. The type, never the rule's id, is how to recognise the pay rule, the office rule and so on. The pay rule holds its minimum as `floor` {`amount` (yearly), `currency` (ISO code), `basis`: `total` or `base`}: judge pay only in that currency and as a yearly figure; another currency, or a day or hourly rate, is unknown, never a fail, and never converted. Retired rule ids keep their names in `retiredRules`.

**Who the user is, for wording.** `profile/me` holds `country`, `location`, `timezone`, `spelling` (UK or US), `profession`, `roleShort` (e.g. "PM") and `fieldTerm` (e.g. "product"). Work out "today" in `timezone`. Never assume a country, a currency or a profession.

## Answers to questions

A question can carry an answer. Answered questions sit in an **Answered** fold on the Questions tab; the open list and the tab's count show only unanswered ones. The question lists themselves (`enrich.openQuestions`, notes' `nextQuestions`, company and sector `questions`) are unchanged — keep writing them as plain strings.

- **Where the answer lives:** role questions (and notes' `nextQuestions`) on the **role**; company questions **and sector questions** on the **company**, because a sector question gets a different answer at each company.
- **`qAnswers`** (role or company): array of `{q, a, at, src:"you"|"notes", convId}`. `q` is the exact question text; matching is trimmed and case-insensitive. Removing the entry reopens the question.
- **`qSuggest`** (role only): proposed answers found in meeting notes, waiting for the user — `{q, scope:"role"|"company", sid, a, convId, date, at}`. Accept files it into the right `qAnswers`; Dismiss drops it. **Never write straight to `qAnswers` from notes without their yes** — a wrong match would quietly close a real question.
- When notes are logged on the board, it asks Claude which open questions they answer and adds `qSuggest` items; "Check all my notes now" on the Questions tab does the same for older notes. `next-role-meetings` does it when notes are logged in a chat.
- An answer that bears on a deal-breaker or preference shows a "May change …, review Fit" nudge. Fit is never changed automatically.

# Next Role Board Rules

Where every piece of information goes on the Next Role job-search board (the Claude artifact).
**Any session that writes to the board follows this page** — the scheduled tasks' skills, and any
chat where the user says "add this to the board". The skills point here rather than repeating it.

The skills that work this board all start `next-role-` (sweep, shortlist, role-fit, apply-pack, interview-prep, meetings). Their manifest — trigger, what each reads and writes — is `refs/skills`, shown on How to use › Under the hood.

## A question is a question

Anything in `enrich.openQuestions` (role), `questions` (company), `askThem` (prep) or a
conversation's `nextQuestions` must:
- end in "?", and be one question;
- be short — about 12 words, the minimum for the user to know what to ask;
- leave the background (evidence, reasoning, numbers) in research or a note.

If a line from the user's notes is a to-do or a fact, move it to the right field — never rewrite it
as a question.

## Keep it short

The board is read on a phone. Every research field, on companies, roles and sectors alike:
- **Leads with the verdict.** "Healthy and well funded: …", not the evidence first.
- **Two sentences at most, under about 40 words.** Company and sector `summary` is two lines.
- **List items** (upside, red flags, questions) **under about 12 words.**
- **No sources, dates or working-out inline.** If the detail is worth keeping, it goes in `notes`.
- Short fact fields (size, HQ, sites, warm route, why watched) are a phrase, not a sentence.
- **Plain English in the user's spelling** (`profile/me` `spelling`: UK or US), in research, prep, answers and packs.
- **Write to the user as "you".** The user reads every field: never their name, he, she or they — "you have none", not "he has none". Prompts written for another model (the mock interviewer) say "the candidate".

## Where everything else goes

| What it is | Field | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Facts about the company | company fields (`health`, `culture`, `ai`, `comp`, …) | Research → Company |
| Facts about the role | `enrich.*`, `location`, `office`, `salary` | Research → Role |
| A known fact with no field | role `notes` `[{at,text}]` — append only, never edit or remove the user's | Research → Notes |
| Questions for them, this role | `enrich.openQuestions` | Questions tab |
| Questions true of every role at the company | company `questions` | Questions tab |
| Interviews, other meetings and tasks | `commitments` — one per interview, `state: "unplanned"` until booked; advice in its `prep`. Process research in `interviewIntel.stages` | Role card → Interviews; Week ahead |
| Prep themes, things to have a view on | `interviewGeneral.themes` | Interviews → Every interview |
| What happened in a meeting, follow-ups, things to brush up | conversation `liked` / `concerned` / `notes` / `nextStep`, with `meetingId` | The meeting's notes, wherever the meeting shows |
| Who the user is — name, location, profession, availability, CV facts | `profile/me` | About me → Static info, and the mock interviewer |
| What the user wants — hard rules, scores, flags, interview questions | `profile/prefs` (`hardRules`, `scored`, `upside`, `red`, `interview`, `decisions`, `roleShape`) | About me › My criteria. The source of truth; skills read it |
| Where roles come from — channels and the sources inside them | `channels` and `sources` (`status`: active / trial / dropped, `why`, `note`) | Sourcing |
| Roles the user adds | Shortlist › Add roles: one role, pasted links, or "Nothing new" (a `runs` doc, `type: "manual"`). Pasted rows: `readState` waiting / read / needs + `readReason` (login, gone, blocked, notfound), `readTries`, `pasted`, `titleGuess` | Shortlist; Sourcing › Manual lists the passes, worked out from these |
| People the user knows | `people` (`name`, `how`, `role`, `companyId` or `company`, `linkedin`, `note`). Meetings link by `personIds` on the commitment (names copied into `person`) | People, with their meetings and tasks; company card → People |
| Pay and where it came from | role `pay.base` / `pay.total` = `{value, kind: stated or estimate, source}`; offers in `offer.*`. Stated = the ad, a recruiter or interviewer; estimate = salary data, source and date named | Compare, Shortlist card; the pay deal-breaker (type `pay`) fails only on a stated figure or an offer, in its floor's currency |
| An offer's real numbers | role `offer.*` (`base`, `bonus`, `total`, `pension`, `holiday`, `office`, `start`, `deadline`, `note`) — they replace the research estimates | Compare |
| Fun and Shot | Required before a role leaves the longlist (accept) or the shortlist (Send to prep); the board asks for them | Longlist, Shortlist, Mass review |
| Where a role was found | role `channelId` + `sourceId` (`co:<companyId>` for a careers page, `flag:<term>` for a flag search, `ch:<channelId>` when no particular source in that channel). Required on every new role | Research → Role; Insights |
| How much the user wants a company or sector | `priority`: high / medium / low / unrated (Want it / Would consider / If it appears) — one scale for both. For a company it also sets how often the sweep fetches its job board: Want it every sweep, Would consider weekly, If it appears and unrated never (unrated is not searched until rated, so the fetched list only grows by the user's decision). Only the user sets it. Off the list = `listing` excluded / defunct / rejected, chosen as the rating with a reason (`offNote`); kept, never deleted | Rating on the card; About me › My criteria |

## How the records link

```
sector ← company.sectorId ← role.companyId ← commitment.forKind/forId (+ tagRoles, personIds)
                                     ↑                         ↑
                    conversation.roleId / companyId / sectorId   conversation.meetingId
```

- `company.sector` is a free-text description; the link to a sector card is `company.sectorId`. Set it when the company clearly sits in a sector we keep a card for — the sector's questions then show on every role there.
- A conversation names the narrowest thing it is about: `roleId` (its company is implied), else `companyId`, else `sectorId`. Add `meetingId` when it came from a logged meeting.
- Roles on the longlist often have no company record; one is created at the shortlist research pass. That is by design, not a break.
- Deleting a meeting, company or sector on the board clears the links pointing at it.

## Meetings and tasks (rebuilt 1 Oct, evening)

Every meeting and task is one `commitments` document. Interview stages no longer exist as a separate record.

- `item`: `meeting` (time, `duration` in minutes, people) or `task` (a due `date` only).
- `forKind` + `forId`: what it is for — `role`, `company`, `sector`, `person`, `meeting` (tasks only, e.g. prep for that meeting) or `none`. A role item also sets `roleId`. A meeting can tag more roles in `tagRoles` so it shows on those cards too (e.g. a recruiter call pitching two roles is for the recruiter, tagged with both).
- `type` (the label in brackets is what the board shows):
  - Role meetings: `informal` (Informal chat), `screen` (Recruiter screen), `hm` (Hiring manager interview), `domain`, `sense` (Product sense / design), `competency`, `culture`, `panel`, `livecase` (Live case study), `casepres` (Case study presentation), `exec` (Exec / founder chat), `test` (Test / assessment), `ref` (Reference / offer call).
  - Company: `coffee`, `info`. Sector: `event`, `info`. Person: `recintro`, `recchk`, `catchup`. Nothing: `training`, `mentoring`, `mock`, `other`.
  - Tasks: `prep`, `takehome`, `onlinetest`, `pack`, `followup`, `chase`, `research`, `practice`, `othertask`.
  - Older items with `interview` / `conversation` still read as Interview / Informal chat.
- People: `personIds` point at `people` docs; `person` holds their names for display. A new person is created as a `people` doc first.
- An interview not yet booked is a role meeting with `state: "unplanned"` and no date; it shows as Not planned. Undated items keep their order in `order`. Booking it fills the same document — never add a second one of the same type for the role.
- **Prep advice lives on the meeting**, in `prep`: `kind: "screen"` uses the screen fields (`tellMe`, `proofPoint`, `whyRole`, `whyCompany`, `likelyQuestions`, `avoid`, `askThem`, `salary`, `logistics`); `kind: "round"` uses `tests`, `focus`, `stories`, `avoid`, `likelyQuestions`, `askThem`, `type` (mock type) and `mock {type, focus}`. Never write `screenPrep` or `interviewPrep` on the role again — the board moves any it finds onto a meeting.
- The prep *task* for a booked meeting is derived: `prepLead` days before (0 = none), ticked with `prepDone`. It follows the meeting until the user moves the prep; then `prepOn` (a date, the meeting's own day allowed) holds it. Moving a meeting never touches `prepOn`, and moving the prep never moves the meeting.
- A conversation about a meeting carries `meetingId` = that commitment's id.
- **Repeating items**: one document per series, `state: "recurring"`, `repeatEvery` week / fortnight / month, `repeatDays` (0 Sun .. 6 Sat; week and fortnight), `repeatDate` (1-31; month — a shorter month uses its last day), `startsOn` (the fortnight counts from its week), optional `endsOn`; meetings also carry `time` and `duration`. Occurrences are worked out by the board; ticks are in `doneDates`, written only by the board. No `prepLead`.

## Interview materials

What a company gives the user to prepare: one `materials` doc each — `title`, `kind` (link / text / file), `url`, `text` (up to 20,000 characters), `file` {id, name, size, type} (an asset in the board's file store, up to 5 MB: PDF, image, Markdown or plain text), `converted` {from, name, size} (set when the board turned a Word file into Markdown), `textFrom: "extracted"` (set when `text` is next-role-interview-prep's copy of the file), `note`, `addedAt`, and the scope: `scopeKind` company (every role there) / role (all its interviews) / meeting, with `companyId`, `roleId`, `meetingId`.
- Added on the role's Interviews tab or the company card. The form offers pasted text first, then a link, then a file. Word (.docx, up to 20 MB) is converted to Markdown in the browser and only the Markdown is stored. PowerPoint is refused with a prompt to save it as PDF. Files over 5 MB and text over 20,000 characters are refused; the user brings them to Claude in chat ("summarise this interview material for #N") and Claude saves a short `text` version.
- Storage: How to use › Under the hood shows a storage meter: file-store bytes and file count against its quota (owner only), board-data size and record count (no overall cap is published), and the largest record against the 256 KB per-record limit.
- `digest` {builtAt, format, assesses[], questions[], points[]} is written by next-role-interview-prep and is what the Mock interview tab gives the interviewer. The company's own materials outrank every source except the user's conversation notes.

## When a role ends

Every ending records **who** ended it and **why** — `endBy`, `endReason`, `endNote`, `endStage`, `endAt` on the role (the stage-specific fields `g1Reason` / `g2Reason` / `closedReason` are still written with the same reason, for the sweep's longlist fold).

The reasons are the user's own, in `profile/settings` `roles.endReasons`, one list for each `endBy`, most used first:
- `me` — I said no (every longlist and shortlist pass, or withdrawing later);
- `them` — they said no;
- `neither` — it went away.

The board always keeps Fails one of my must-haves, Needs something I don't have, Chose another route, Went quiet, Role pulled or filled and Other. One reason only — the biggest; the rest goes in the note. (Older rows keep their previous reason in `endReasonPrev`.)

- **Fails one of my must-haves**: also record which deal-breaker it fails as `endRule` (a rule id), or add the rule first if none fits. It got past the sweep, so that rule's check note is what to improve.
- **Needs something I don't have**: also record what they require as `endGap`, using the name from `profile/me` `gaps` (add it there if new). Role Fit always marks it a gap; CVs and prep never claim it.
- *Other* always needs a note. The shortlist always needs a note.
- `endStage` is set automatically: "Gate 1" (longlist), "Gate 2" (shortlist) — stored words kept — After applying, After interviewing (plus `endStagesDone`).
- Older rows and the folded longlist tallies use the previous reason words; the board maps them onto these lists when it reads them. Do not rewrite them.

## Week ahead (commitments)

Week ahead has two tabs, Calendar and Pending. Which one a commitment lands on is decided by its `state`, never by a tag:

| `state` | Tab |
|---|---|
| `booked` / `done` | Calendar (a booked date in the past shows as "Not logged") |
| `offered` | Pending — waiting on a person's reply. Shows "<Name>'s reply · N days" since `lastChased` or `sentAt`; moves to "Chase now" at the top once `chaseBy` passes. Set `sentAt`, `chaseBy`, `person` |
| `conditional` | Pending — waiting on an event. Always set `blockedBy` to two or three words (e.g. "Screen feedback"); the full sentence goes in `condition` |
| `recurring` | Calendar, on its `repeatDays` |
| `unplanned` | Pending → Not planned yet — offered or added by the user but not booked, or a task with no date. With `expected: true` (a round the company's process says comes next that nobody has offered yet; skills set it on meetings and tasks they create) it stays off Week ahead and shows only on the role's Interviews tab as "Expected, not offered". Only the user clears it, by booking it or setting it to waiting on their reply |
| any open state, role ended | Off Week ahead: when a role is closed or rejected, the board closes its unplanned, offered and conditional items (meetings Cancelled, tasks Won't do; `closedWhy: "role closed"`). Never create a meeting or task for an ended role |

Tasks show on their due day; an unfinished one carries forward to today as Overdue. The board also shows two automatic deadlines, not stored: a role's `closing` date (Shortlist and To apply) and an offer's `offer.deadline`.

## Sweep checks
- Companies may carry `officeDays` (days a week) and `officeNote`. The sweep reads them when it checks the office-days deal-breaker and preference, as their check notes say.
- Every `linkChecked` date comes with `linkMethod`: `index` (found in the employer's list of current openings) or `browser`. No method, no date.

## Closing gone roles
- A role needs its own job link (the ATS job id page). Search pages, board front pages and search-engine hits are not role links; search-engine finds are treated as aggregator finds.
- For roles outside the office deal-breaker's range (type `office`) the sweep reads the full posting for office days and writes them to `office` and the company's `officeDays`.
- The morning next-role-daily-check run re-checks every longlist role against its employer's index and closes the ones that have gone (`endBy: neither`, Role pulled or filled). The only reject made without the user.

## Role numbers
- Every role has `ref`, a unique number shown after its title as #N, so the user can name a role in chat ("#74").
- The board assigns the next number to any role without one when it loads. Skills never write or change `ref`.
- When the user says "#N", find the role with `ref == N`.

## Aggregator roles - liveness
- An aggregator find is checked against the employer board's index of current openings. Not in the index: never written to the board; logged in the run's `screened` doc as `gone from employer board`.
- Employer board unreachable: written to the longlist with `liveCheck: "you"` and the red flag "Check it's live - couldn't reach <company>'s job board". The board shows a "Check it's live" chip; the user checks it.
- When verified, `url` is the employer's posting, not the aggregator's.

ats-endpoints.title: ATS endpoints and careers-site search
ats-endpoints.md:
## 1b. ATS JSON board endpoints - check the list, not the page

**The company-led axis reads these, not the HTML careers page.** A board listing rendered as HTML is
5k-50k tokens of markup wrapping what is really a list of titles and locations; the JSON endpoint is a
fraction of that. With dozens of companies read every sweep, that difference is most of the sweep's cost.

**This does not weaken the liveness rule.** The rule is that a single job *page* cannot establish that a
posting is open - a dead Teamtailor requisition still serves its body, and a dead Greenhouse one redirects
to a form. A board *index* is the permitted source, and that is exactly what these are: the employer's own
list of what is open right now.

| ATS | JSON endpoint | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Greenhouse** | `boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<slug>/jobs` | **Verified.** Carries `title`, `location`, `absolute_url`, `updated_at`, `first_published`, `id`. **No descriptions unless you add `?content=true`** - do not add it |
| **Lever** | `api.lever.co/v0/postings/<slug>?mode=json` | **Verified.** Carries `text` (title), `categories` (location, team, commitment), `hostedUrl`, `createdAt`. **Includes the full description and there is no way to turn it off**, so it is heavier per role - acceptable because most Lever boards are small |
| **Ashby** | `api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/<slug>` | **Verified.** Carries `title`, `location`, `isRemote`, `employmentType`, `publishedAt`, `jobUrl`, plus descriptions |
| **Workable** | `apply.workable.com/api/v1/widget/accounts/<slug>` | **Unverified** - a guessed slug returned 404 in testing, which tests the slug rather than the endpoint. **Probe it once, and fall back to the HTML board if it 404s** |
| **Teamtailor** | - | No public token-free endpoint found. Use the HTML board |

**Rules when using these:**

- **Find the slug from the HTML board URL** on the company's card - `job-boards.greenhouse.io/acme` gives `acme`.
- **A 404 is not a dead company.** It means the slug or the endpoint pattern is wrong. Fall back to the HTML board that run, and record the working URL on the company row so the next run does not repeat the guess.
- **Never add a parameter that returns descriptions** where the API lets you opt out. The list pass only needs title, location and date; the full posting is fetched only for a role that survives the hard rules.

## 1c. Reading one ad - when the page loads with JavaScript

**Some careers sites build the ad in the browser** (Oracle, Workday, SuccessFactors, iCIMS, SmartRecruiters). A plain fetch of the job page returns a near-empty shell: a cookie banner, a title, no description. The page itself loads the ad from the site's own feed, and that feed can be fetched directly, no browser needed.

**The rule (longlist research, shortlist, and the sweep when it reads a full posting):**

1. Fetch the job page as usual. If it carries the description, use it.
2. If it comes back near-empty (no responsibilities or requirements, only a title, banner or script), match the link's host to a pattern below, build the feed address from the link, and fetch that.
3. No pattern for the host, or the feed fails too: don't score from the fragment. Set `readState: "needs"`, `readReason: "nofeed"` and `readHost` (the link's host, e.g. `fa-evdq-saasfaprod1.fa.ocs.oraclecloud.com`). Leave Role Fit rough and deal-breakers unknown. The board lists these under Data health, Job sites we can't read yet, and next-role-fix works out the pattern.
4. A feed read is the posting, never proof the role is open: `linkChecked` still comes only from a board index or a real browser.

| ATS | Host looks like | Job link looks like | Feed address | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Oracle Recruiting Cloud** | `*.fa.*.oraclecloud.com` | `https://<host>/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/<site>/job/<id>` | `https://<host>/hcmRestApi/resources/latest/recruitingCEJobRequisitionDetails?onlyData=true&expand=all&finder=ById%3BId%3D%22<id>%22%2CsiteNumber%3D<site>` (encode `;`, `=`, `"`, `,` as shown) | **Verified** - full description returned |

Add a row only after reading a real ad through it with a plain fetch. next-role-fix finds the feed by opening one flagged ad in the browser and reading its network calls.

## 2. ATS site-scoped search - a technique, not a site

**Often finds roles no job board carries.** Search location strings like these against `job-boards.greenhouse.io`, `jobs.ashbyhq.com` and `jobs.lever.co`. The examples are for the UK; use the person's own country and city (`profile/me`) in the same patterns:

- `"Remote, United Kingdom"`
- `"Remote Eligible in UK"`
- `"| UK | Remote"`
- `"GB - United Kingdom"`
- `"Hybrid/Remote (UK)"`

**This is the one channel that finds roles no board carries**, because it reads the applicant tracking system directly rather than waiting for a board to index it.
